cost_realism_ruling.question_put_to_the_director: Should FUTURES_EXECUTION_COST_REALITY - a per-market futures execution cost table built from owned Norgate volume and open interest - be a PRE-REQUISITE data-foundation assignment for R65, so the table must exist and be certified BEFORE any futures cell is scored? Or may the cells run on the current flat futures rate with the per-market table as a follow-on re-test?
cost_realism_ruling.ruling: NEITHER OPTION AS PUT. The question contains a false premise, and the correct answer is a THIRD one, which is stricter than the follow-on and cheaper than the prerequisite. Recorded as: PER_MARKET_COST_MANDATORY_AT_SCORING, OBSERVED_COST_TABLE_MANDATORY_AT_CLEARING.
cost_realism_ruling.the_false_premise: There is no 'current flat futures rate' in the governed path, and no R65 cell could run on one. (a) The R38 native contract layer already carries a PER-MARKET cost_bps_per_side vector of 2-15 bp (NEXT_CAMPAIGN_CENSUS.json#available_pit_datasets). (b) R60's own frozen cost model, read out of the memory row H_e490a5b8_5c87b7dbcae0, is cost_model_id FUTURES_PER_MARKET_R38_PLUS_ROLL_V1 with rate_per_side 'per market, 2-15 bp (MODELLED_NOT_OBSERVED)' and roll_cost 'charged, interior and at entry'. (c) alpha_agent\r61\cost_budget.py:201-221 refuses structurally to coerce that prose into a number, and its docstring says why in terms: 'a reader that coerced that to 0.0 would wave every futures cell through on a cost of nothing'. A caller supplying neither a vector nor a measured effective rate gets COST_BUDGET_NOT_EVALUABLE, and that state FAILS for every governed caller. The flat-rate risk named in the R59 memory entry is a property of futures_panel_v1, the back-adjusted panel. This agenda places all three cells on the R38 native layer, so that exposure does not arise.
what_is_binding_at_SCORING: Every R65 cell is scored under the R38 PER-MARKET cost vector plus a charged roll cost. No cell may be scored at a uniform rate across markets.

Where the budget needs a scalar, it MUST be the notional-weighted effective rate from alpha_agent.r61.cost_budget.effective_cost_per_side(traded_notional_per_instrument, cost_per_side_vector). Charging the cheapest market's rate flatters the cell; charging the dearest kills it; the weighted rate is the only honest scalar.

additional_ann_cost_drag MUST carry the roll cost explicitly and may not be left at its 0.0 default. The estate has its own measurement of the size of this term: the R60 cross-asset futures cell H_e490a5b8_5c87b7dbcae0 recorded ann_roll_cost_drag 0.010163 against ann_rebalance_cost_drag 0.003641 at a mean one-way turnover of 0.2336. ROLL COST WAS 2.8x THE REBALANCE COST. A futures cell that omits it understates its burden by more than it reports.
A cell whose instrument set cannot be mapped onto the R38 per-market vector HALTS as COST_BUDGET_NOT_EVALUABLE. It does not fall back to an average.
cost_realism_ruling.what_is_binding_at_CLEARING: The observed per-market cost table (FUTURES_EXECUTION_COST_REALITY, free_proxy = owned Norgate volume and open interest, gate_verdict NO_PURCHASE_REQUIRED) is a BLOCKING PRE-CONDITION on director_clear. The director pre-commits, now and before any R65 result exists: no R65 cell may be ruled CLEARED, and no forward registration may be raised on one, until (i) that table exists and is certified by the data-foundation-agent, (ii) the survivor is re-scored under it through cost_budget.effective_cost_per_side, and (iii) it still passes the frozen 0.03/yr ceiling and the qualification gate. Pre-committing this before results is what makes it a governance rule rather than a post-hoc reason to kill an inconvenient survivor.
reasoning_on_the_asymmetry: The asymmetry is real and it is decisive AT THE CLEARING BOUNDARY, not at the scoring boundary. A false positive here would be the estate's FIRST survivor in ~8,413 tests. It would carry enormous evidential weight precisely because it is unique, and it is the only kind of artifact that travels toward a capital decision. A false negative costs one burden slot and is already, by R61's own finding, the expected outcome of almost any cell on these panels.

But a prerequisite BUILD before scoring buys very little and costs a lot. The estate is not exposed to a flat rate today (see the false premise), so the marginal improvement the observed table offers is a refinement of a 2-15 bp modelled vector, not the removal of a uniform one. Making it a prerequisite would stall three cells behind a data build, and a data build that stalls a campaign is how R60's budget was exhausted (docs\RELEASE61_RESEARCH_APPARATUS_CALIBRATION.md lines 300-308).

A pure follow-on re-test is ALSO wrong, and for a reason the question does not name: a re-test is a NEW pre-registration charged to the burden. 'Run flat now, re-test later' therefore spends the slot twice on one idea and would breach the three-variants cap on the second pass. Holding the re-test as a CLEARING pre-condition avoids that: re-scoring an already-measured cell under a stricter cost model is an ADVERSARIAL check on an existing candidate, not a new hypothesis.

The estate already owns a partial guard and it is made BLOCKING here rather than advisory: alpha_agent.agents_v2.runner.adversarial_pack computes a DOUBLED_COST re-score. At 2x the modelled per-market vector that brackets roughly 4-30 bp/side, which covers most of the plausible observed range for these instrument sets. For every R65 futures cell, a failure of the doubled-cost adversarial check is a KILL, not a note.

One honesty point that cuts against the director's own ruling and is recorded rather than hidden: the R38 vector is stamped MODELLED_NOT_OBSERVED in the frozen R60 cost model. The estate therefore does not currently know its own futures execution costs from observation, and has recorded that as an open gap. This ruling does not close that gap; it prevents the gap from ever converting into a cleared survivor.

cells.label: FUT_INTL_INDEX_OPEN_INTEREST_GROWTH_COST_HONEST
cells.economic_mechanism_plain_english: When lots of new money piles into a stock-index futures market - open interest climbing faster than its own recent norm - that market is getting crowded. Crowded positions are the ones that have to be unwound in a hurry, and the unwinding pushes the price the other way. So we bet AGAINST the index futures markets whose open interest has grown fastest, and FOR the ones where it has shrunk. If the mechanism is real it is a crowding-and-unwind effect, not a forecast of economic news.

cells.label: XA_METALS_TO_COMMODITY_CURRENCY_LEAD_LAG_H3
cells.economic_mechanism_plain_english: Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Norway and Chile export metals and energy. When the price of industrial metals jumps hard, those countries have just become richer, and their currencies should follow. The bet is that the currency does not reprice in the same instant the metal does - that it takes a few days for the information to cross from the commodity pit to the currency market. So: on the rare days when industrial metals make a big move, buy the commodity currencies if metals jumped and sell them if metals fell, hold three sessions, and be in cash the rest of the time. If the currency market is efficient across asset classes, this pays nothing.

cells.pre_registered_construction: ONE channel, declared entirely in advance. LEAD: an equal-weighted industrial-metals composite of the certified R38 industrial metals markets, its 3-session return measured to t. TRIGGER: the book takes a position only when the absolute value of that 3-session composite return sits in the TOP DECILE of its own trailing 252-session distribution computed from data at or before t. On all other decisions the book is FLAT, and a flat decision earns and costs nothing. LAG: the certified commodity-currency futures (AUD, CAD, NZD, NOK and any other certified commodity exporter), rank-weighted long/short in the SIGN of the metals move, entered at the next available session and held 3 sessions. OBSERVABILITY: metals and FX futures trade on different calendars; the signal instant is the last session on which BOTH the metals composite and the traded currency are quoted at or before t, and any market missing that session is not scorable on that decision. The top-decile trigger is declared HERE, before any turnover or any return has been seen; it is the parameter that sets how often the book trades and it may not be moved afterwards.

pre_registered_cost_budget.the_binding_constraint: At a 3-session hold the book re-forms 84 times a year - seven times as often as a monthly book - so cost, not signal, is the binding constraint. Computed through the owner: with a 0.20%/yr roll charge, the MAXIMUM mean one-way turnover per period that stays inside the 0.03/yr ceiling is 0.3333 at a 5 bp effective rate, 0.1667 at 10 bp, and 0.1111 at 15 bp. A continuously-invested h3 futures book would breach the ceiling outright: 0.35 one-way at 5 bp plus 0.20%/yr roll measures 0.0314/yr and returns COST_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.
pre_registered_cost_budget.why_the_construction_can_still_be_expres: Only because the book is SPARSE BY DESIGN. A top-decile trigger puts it in the market on roughly one decision in ten, so its mean one-way turnover per period - which is what the budget charges - is expected in the 0.10-0.25 band, and its roll exposure is proportionally smaller than a fully-invested book's. This is a PROJECTION, not a measurement, and it is written down so it can be wrong in public.
pre_registered_cost_budget.roll_cost_evidence: The estate's own measured roll drag on a cross-asset futures book is 1.016%/yr (H_e490a5b8_5c87b7dbcae0, D layer, ann_roll_cost_drag 0.010163) at a mean one-way turnover of 0.2336. Roll was 2.8x the rebalance cost on that book. A sparse book pays proportionally less, but it must CHARGE it, and additional_ann_cost_drag may not be 0.0.

pre_registered_halt_conditions: COST_BUDGET: this is the cell's most likely death and it is declared as such. If the measured mean one-way turnover per period at the measured notional-weighted effective per-market rate, plus the charged roll, exceeds 0.03/yr, HALT COST_BUDGET_EXCEEDED before any return is scored. The director expects this outcome to be more likely than any alpha finding, and says so now.

TRIGGER RATE: if the top-decile trigger fires on fewer decisions than r59.OBS_FLOOR (36) in any of the three layers, the layer has no defensible statistic and the cell HALTS as UNDERPOWERED_BY_CONSTRUCTION. Floor frozen here.

EFFECTIVE OBSERVATIONS: the runner's own effective_observations against r59.OBS_FLOOR is binding per layer. A 3-session horizon on a 3-session cadence is non-overlapping, so the overlap_factor correction should be near 1; if it is not, the runner's number wins and the director's expectation does not.

CALENDAR: if the mixed-calendar rule leaves a currency unscorable on more than 20% of triggered decisions, HALT as DATA_HOLD rather than filling forward. A forward-filled cross-calendar price is a look-ahead.
STAGE ADVANCE: stage_advance is the sole authority. A halt at D or V settles as recorded.
SIGN: expected_sign is +1 (metals up implies commodity currency up) and is frozen. A reversal-shaped result is a FAILURE, not a reversal hypothesis.

refused.label: XA_METALS_TO_COMMODITY_CURRENCY_LEAD_LAG_H3
refused.refused_by: quant-research-director. This is a DIRECTOR refusal, not a pipeline refusal: preregister was NOT attempted, because with features published, data certified, the family routed and the sign declared it would very likely have SUCCEEDED, minting an id and charging the CROSS_ASSET burden denominator forever for a cell the director had already judged un-freezable. Attempting it would have been the harm.
blocking_reasons: 1. THE DECLARED LEAD VARIABLE COLLAPSED TO ONE MARKET. The director froze 'an equal-weighted industrial-metals composite of the certified R38 industrial metals markets'; fs_r65_02 itself lists copper, aluminium, zinc, nickel and tin as typical members. The published universe r65_xa_metals_currency_leadlag delivers 'equal-weighted composite of certified industrial metals (HG copper)' - n=1. A one-market composite is copper, not industrial metals, and that is a change to the ECONOMIC MECHANISM, not to a parameter. A broad industrial-metals demand shock and a copper move are different hypotheses.

2. THE COLLAPSE CREATES AN IDENTITY COLLISION THE DIRECTOR DID NOT PRE-DECLARE. The memory already holds H_06816d6f_f09c738cd8b7, 'R46 challenger r52_rates_copper_gold_lead', input_data_identity '&ZN, signed by the one-quarter change in ln(&HG/&GC) - the copper/gold ratio', family CROSS_ASSET_LEAD_LAG, outcome FORWARD_FROZEN. A copper-move-signs-another-asset lead-lag channel is ALREADY REGISTERED FORWARD in this estate. The skeptic focus the director requested was against the dollar-beta row H_e490a5b8_5c87b7dbcae0; the copper collapse creates a much nearer relative that was never pre-declared as the thing to attack.

3. THE OBSERVABILITY INSTANT IS UNRESOLVED, AND THE ARTIFACTS CONTRADICT EACH OTHER. fs_r65_02 sets lag_sessions 0 on the metals composite and asserts 'Session t (end of day when both metals and FX markets have closed)'. Its OWN limitations concede the opposite: 'Calendar mismatch ... introducing a 1-2 session slippage in some cases.' The universe states 'metals trade US hours, FX trade 24-hour currency futures', and its observability_instant field answers a different question (t-2, for open interest, which this PRICE-based cell never reads). Nowhere is the metals close measured against the FX futures close. For a LEAD-LAG cell the entire economic claim IS the lag: if the number of sessions between the signal instant and the first earned return is unmeasured, the cell cannot be distinguished from a one-session look-ahead. At h21 that is a 5% nuisance; at h3, against the book's ret[t+1 : t+1+horizon] convention, it is a third of the horizon and 100% of the mechanism. This is the same defect - an unmeasured publication lag on the signal leg - for which the director refused XA_TERMS_OF_TRADE_RELATIVE_VALUE, and it is refused here for the same reason.

4. THE DIRECTOR'S OWN CALENDAR HALT IS WIRED TO THE WRONG QUANTITY. The frozen halt was 'if the mixed-calendar rule leaves a currency unscorable on more than 20% of TRIGGERED decisions, HALT as DATA_HOLD'. Both published artifacts express currency scorability in terms of OPEN INTEREST coverage, while fs_r65_02 states plainly 'This feature reads PRICES (returns), not OI'. The halt therefore guards a check this cell never performs.
refused.what_the_director_did_not_do: Did not set lag_sessions to 1, did not edit a published feature set, did not add a halt condition after the fact, and did not relax anything. Feature computation is owned by the feature-library-agent and the campaign executor module; a parameter change made here would be a NEW experiment, and a director quietly repairing a feature set is the hidden tuning this contract forbids.
refused.remedy: feature-library-agent re-publishes fs_r65_02 at a new version with (a) a lead variable that is genuinely a multi-market industrial-metals composite, or an honestly relabelled single-market copper channel carrying a pre-declared identity check against H_06816d6f_f09c738cd8b7, and (b) a DERIVED observability instant in the shape the OI cells already use ('exchange OI for session s published s+1, signal lag s, union = s+2'), measuring the metals close against the FX futures close rather than asserting the question away. Only then can the director freeze and mint it.

plain_english.what_this_campaign_is: Three small, cheap experiments in markets that are NOT US stocks. Nothing here touches real money, places an order, or changes anything the system does. It is research, and the most likely result - by a wide margin - is that all three find nothing.
plain_english.why_only_three: We were offered room for four. We used three. The fourth idea we would have run sits on a data source that our own data team marked 'on hold, not measured', and running an experiment on data nobody has checked is how you get a confident wrong answer. An unused slot costs nothing. A used one makes every future result harder to believe, forever.
plain_english.cell_1_in_one_sentence: When too much money crowds into a stock-index futures market, bet against it - because crowded trades have to be unwound, and unwinding moves prices the other way.
plain_english.cell_2_in_one_sentence: Metal-exporting countries get richer when metal prices jump, so on the rare days metals move hard, buy their currencies for three days and sit in cash the rest of the time.
plain_english.cell_3_in_one_sentence: The same crowding bet as cell 1, but in commodities - sell the ones where the crowd is piling in fastest, buy the ones it is leaving.
plain_english.what_we_honestly_expect: Nothing. The house has now run about 8,400 of these tests and not one has passed. Last year we finally measured WHY, and the answer was uncomfortable: our machinery can only reliably see an edge worth roughly 3% to 6.5% a year after costs, and most real market edges are smaller than that. None of these three ideas is likely to be that big. We are running them anyway for a specific reason, stated below.
plain_english.why_run_them_at_all: Two of the three were killed last year by a rule that turned out to be wrong. It priced futures trades as though they cost as much as trading mid-sized company shares, which they do not - by a factor of five. Those two experiments were shut down before they produced a single number. That rule has since been rebuilt, and the rebuild is locked in by tests so nobody can quietly loosen it later. Running these two finishes the job. Whatever they say, we will have a number instead of a gap. The third is a genuinely new idea in the one corner of the map our own records still list as unexplored.
plain_english.the_promise_we_are_making_in_advance: If an experiment comes back empty AND the edge it was looking for was smaller than our machinery can see, we will write it down as 'we could not have seen it', NOT as 'it isn't there'. Those are different statements and the difference matters. We are writing this rule down now, before we have any results, so we cannot choose the flattering interpretation afterwards.
plain_english.the_cost_question_in_plain_terms: Trading costs vary a lot between futures markets - a heavily traded contract is cheap, a thin one is expensive, and the gap is about five to one. If we priced them all the same, a thin market could look like a free lunch when it is nothing of the kind. Our records already vary the cost by market, so we are not making that mistake today. But those per-market costs are ESTIMATED, not observed. So we have committed, in advance: we will not declare ANY of these three a success until we have built the observed cost table from data we already own and re-checked the winner against it. A false alarm is the one mistake this programme cannot afford, because it would be our first ever apparent success and everyone would believe it.
plain_english.what_nobody_is_being_asked_to_do: Nobody is being asked to approve anything, buy any data, spend any money, or trade anything. This document freezes what we will test and how we will judge it, before we test it.
